lec05kp10en-u01-p1-title.name: u01-p1-title
lec05kp10en-u01-p1-title.text: A perfect training score need not survive new data

lec05kp10en-u01-p1-bridge.name: u01-p1-bridge
lec05kp10en-u01-p1-bridge.text: Earlier networks classified given points. What should judge a network meant for unseen points?

lec05kp10en-u01-p1-next-question.name: u01-p1-next-question
lec05kp10en-u01-p1-next-question.text: Which adjustable numbers give three hidden units their flexibility?

lec05kp10en-u01-p1-fig1.name: fig:lec05-kp10-trend
lec05kp10en-u01-p1-fig1.text: 同一批帶雜訊的樣本與平滑規律；折線僅作教學示意，不是網路訓練結果。

image.alt: A smooth sine trend and six illustrative noisy samples; the piecewise interpolant is not a fitted neural network.

lec05kp10en-u01-p1-card1.name: term:Generalization
lec05kp10en-u01-p1-card1.text: **Generalization**: Correct prediction on data not used for fitting is generalization; memorizing training answers is different.

lec05kp10en-u01-p1-card2.name: u01-p1-card2
lec05kp10en-u01-p1-card2.text: This continuous-prediction illustration exposes a trade-off also faced in classification. Find the main trend before treating sample fluctuations as rules.

lec05kp10en-u01-p2-title.name: u01-p2-title
lec05kp10en-u01-p2-title.text: Count adjustable parameters before choosing network size

lec05kp10en-u01-p2-bridge.name: u01-p2-bridge
lec05kp10en-u01-p2-bridge.text: Memorizing training answers differs from generalization. Which adjustable numbers give three hidden units their flexibility?

lec05kp10en-u01-p2-next-question.name: u01-p2-next-question
lec05kp10en-u01-p2-next-question.text: Does increasing this count always improve prediction?

lec05kp10en-u01-p2-card1.name: term:Free parameter
lec05kp10en-u01-p2-card1.text: **Free parameter**: A free parameter is an independently adjustable number; weights and biases both count.

lec05kp10en-u01-p2-card2.name: u01-p2-card2
lec05kp10en-u01-p2-card2.text: Use two inputs, three hidden units and one output, with dense connections and one bias per computing unit.

lec05kp10en-u01-p2-card3.name: u01-p2-card3
lec05kp10en-u01-p2-card3.text: Hidden layer: $(2+1)\times3=9$. Output layer: $(3+1)\times1=4$. There are $9+4=13$ parameters, not three.

lec05kp10en-u01-p3-title.name: u01-p3-title
lec05kp10en-u01-p3-title.text: Too little flexibility misses rules; too much can fit noise

lec05kp10en-u01-p3-bridge.name: u01-p3-bridge
lec05kp10en-u01-p3-bridge.text: Our three hidden units use thirteen free parameters. Does increasing this count always improve prediction?

lec05kp10en-u01-p3-next-question.name: u01-p3-next-question
lec05kp10en-u01-p3-next-question.text: Can a fixed architecture do that merely by continuing to train?

lec05kp10en-u01-p3-fig1.name: fig:lec05-kp10-trend
lec05kp10en-u01-p3-fig1.text: 同一批帶雜訊的樣本與平滑規律；折線僅作教學示意，不是網路訓練結果。

image.alt: A smooth sine trend and six illustrative noisy samples; the piecewise interpolant is not a fitted neural network.

lec05kp10en-u01-p3-card1.name: term:Underfitting
lec05kp10en-u01-p3-card1.text: **Underfitting**: Underfitting means the model misses important structure and can perform poorly even on training data.

lec05kp10en-u01-p3-card2.name: term:Overfitting
lec05kp10en-u01-p3-card2.text: **Overfitting**: Overfitting adapts to incidental training details at the expense of prediction on new data.

lec05kp10en-u01-p3-card3.name: u01-p3-card3
lec05kp10en-u01-p3-card3.text: Size alone does not prove overfitting. Data, weight magnitudes, constraints and the fitting procedure also matter.

lec05kp10en-u01-p4-title.name: u01-p4-title
lec05kp10en-u01-p4-title.text: Even a fixed network can worsen with more training

lec05kp10en-u01-p4-bridge.name: u01-p4-bridge
lec05kp10en-u01-p4-bridge.text: Overfitting adapts to incidental training details. Can a fixed architecture do that merely by continuing to train?

lec05kp10en-u01-p4-fig1.name: fig:lec05-kp10-early
lec05kp10en-u01-p4-fig1.text: 五個檢查點的訓練與驗證平均損失；驗證最低在第3輪，訓練最低在第5輪。

image.alt: Training and validation losses at five checkpoints: validation is lowest at epoch three and training at epoch five.

lec05kp10en-u01-p4-card1.name: term:Validation set
lec05kp10en-u01-p4-card1.text: **Validation set**: Validation data do not update weights; they help choose a model or training checkpoint.

lec05kp10en-u01-p4-card2.name: term:Overtraining
lec05kp10en-u01-p4-card2.text: **Overtraining**: Overtraining occurs when further fitting of a fixed architecture starts hurting validation performance.

lec05kp10en-u01-p4-card3.name: u01-p4-card3
lec05kp10en-u01-p4-card3.text: Training loss keeps falling; validation loss rises after its minimum at epoch 3. The curves need not cross or start together.

lec05kp10en-u01-p5-title.name: u01-p5-title
lec05kp10en-u01-p5-title.text: Keep checkpoint 3, not the last checkpoint

lec05kp10en-u01-p5-bridge.name: u01-p5-bridge
lec05kp10en-u01-p5-bridge.text: Validation loss rises after its minimum at epoch 3 while training loss falls. Which checkpoint should we keep?

lec05kp10en-u01-p5-next-question.name: u01-p5-next-question
lec05kp10en-u01-p5-next-question.text: Can repeatedly inspected validation data also give an untouched final score?

lec05kp10en-u01-p5-fig1.name: fig:lec05-kp10-early
lec05kp10en-u01-p5-fig1.text: 五個檢查點的訓練與驗證平均損失；驗證最低在第3輪，訓練最低在第5輪。

image.alt: Training and validation losses at five checkpoints: validation is lowest at epoch three and training at epoch five.

lec05kp10en-u01-p5-card1.name: term:Early stopping
lec05kp10en-u01-p5-card1.text: **Early stopping**: Early stopping uses validation performance and restores the best checkpoint; implementation may allow patience.

lec05kp10en-u01-p5-card2.name: u01-p5-card2
lec05kp10en-u01-p5-card2.text: Validation losses at epochs 1–5 are $0.55,0.35,0.25,0.28,0.40$. The minimum is $0.25$ at epoch 3.

lec05kp10en-u01-p5-card3.name: u01-p5-card3
lec05kp10en-u01-p5-card3.text: Epoch 5 has lower training loss, but validation loss rises from $0.25$ to $0.40$: $0.40-0.25=0.15$.

lec05kp10en-u01-p6-title.name: u01-p6-title
lec05kp10en-u01-p6-title.text: Model selection and final testing need different roles

lec05kp10en-u01-p6-bridge.name: u01-p6-bridge
lec05kp10en-u01-p6-bridge.text: Early stopping restores the best checkpoint, here epoch 3. Can repeatedly inspected validation data also give an untouched final score?

lec05kp10en-u01-p6-next-question.name: u01-p6-next-question
lec05kp10en-u01-p6-next-question.text: With only ten validation cases, how stable is that selection?

lec05kp10en-u01-p6-card2.name: u01-p6-card2
lec05kp10en-u01-p6-card2.text: **Validation data** select size, penalty strength and checkpoints without directly fitting weights.

lec05kp10en-u01-p6-card3.name: term:Test set
lec05kp10en-u01-p6-card3.text: **Test set**: reserve it for evaluation after model selection. Reusing it to choose models breaks independence; avoid duplicate-subject and temporal leakage.

lec05kp10en-u01-p7-title.name: u01-p7-title
lec05kp10en-u01-p7-title.text: A tiny validation set makes selection unstable

lec05kp10en-u01-p7-bridge.name: u01-p7-bridge
lec05kp10en-u01-p7-bridge.text: Training fits weights and validation selects size and checkpoints. With only ten validation cases, how stable is that selection?

lec05kp10en-u01-p7-next-question.name: u01-p7-next-question
lec05kp10en-u01-p7-next-question.text: Can geometry complement this unstable data-based assessment?

lec05kp10en-u01-p7-card1.name: u01-p7-card1
lec05kp10en-u01-p7-card1.text: One error among ten gives $1/10=0.1$; two give $2/10=0.2$. One case changes the estimate by ten percentage points.

lec05kp10en-u01-p7-card2.name: u01-p7-card2
lec05kp10en-u01-p7-card2.text: Repeated splits or cross-validation can support selection, but fitting and evaluation must remain separated. They do not create new independent data.

lec05kp10en-u01-p7-card3.name: u01-p7-card3
lec05kp10en-u01-p7-card3.text: There is no best neuron count independent of the data and task.

lec05kp10en-u01-p8-title.name: u01-p8-title
lec05kp10en-u01-p8-title.text: Geometry counts possible cells, not predictive quality

lec05kp10en-u01-p8-bridge.name: u01-p8-bridge
lec05kp10en-u01-p8-bridge.text: One case changes a ten-case estimate by ten percentage points. Can geometry complement this unstable data-based assessment?

lec05kp10en-u01-p8-next-question.name: u01-p8-next-question
lec05kp10en-u01-p8-next-question.text: Do two parallel XOR boundaries attain the maximum?

lec05kp10en-u01-p8-fig1.name: fig:lec05-kp10-regions
lec05kp10en-u01-p8-fig1.text: 不同輸入維度 d 下，K 個一般位置超平面形成區域數的最大值。

image.alt: Maximum hyperplane cell counts versus hidden-unit count for input dimensions one, two and three.

lec05kp10en-u01-p8-card1.name: term:Cell-count bound
lec05kp10en-u01-p8-card1.text: **Cell-count bound**: K hyperplanes partition d-dimensional space into at most M cells. General position attains the maximum; degenerate arrangements may not.

lec05kp10en-u01-p8-card2.name: u01-p8-card2
lec05kp10en-u01-p8-card2.text: $M_{\max}(K,d)=\sum_{m=0}^{d}\binom{K}{m}$. K counts hidden units and d input dimensions; $\binom{K}{m}=0$ when $m>K$.

lec05kp10en-u01-p8-card3.name: u01-p8-card3
lec05kp10en-u01-p8-card3.text: General position excludes coincidences, parallelism and excessive intersections that reduce cell count; the precise condition depends on dimension.

lec05kp10en-u01-p9-title.name: u01-p9-title
lec05kp10en-u01-p9-title.text: Two planar lines give at most four cells, but parallel lines give three

lec05kp10en-u01-p9-bridge.name: u01-p9-bridge
lec05kp10en-u01-p9-bridge.text: The cell-count bound counts possible cells, not output classes. Do two parallel XOR boundaries attain the maximum?

lec05kp10en-u01-p9-next-question.name: u01-p9-next-question
lec05kp10en-u01-p9-next-question.text: What other routes select network size?

lec05kp10en-u01-p9-fig1.name: fig:lec05-kp10-xor
lec05kp10en-u01-p9-fig1.text: XOR 四點與兩條平行線；實際只有三個區域，不等於一般位置最大值四。

image.alt: Four XOR points and two parallel boundaries enclosing the positive band; three actual cells versus a maximum of four.

lec05kp10en-u01-p9-card1.name: u01-p9-card1
lec05kp10en-u01-p9-card1.text: For $d=2,K=2$, $M_{\max}=1+2+1=4$. The three terms count choices of 0, 1 and 2 lines.

lec05kp10en-u01-p9-card2.name: u01-p9-card2
lec05kp10en-u01-p9-card2.text: The XOR boundaries $x_1+x_2=0.5$ and $x_1+x_2=1.5$ are parallel: three actual bands, with both A points in the middle.

lec05kp10en-u01-p9-card3.name: u01-p9-card3
lec05kp10en-u01-p9-card3.text: An upper bound of four accommodates three cells; sufficiency of two units still needs this explicit construction.

lec05kp10en-u01-p10-title.name: u01-p10-title
lec05kp10en-u01-p10-title.text: Estimate size, prune a large network, or grow a small one

lec05kp10en-u01-p10-bridge.name: u01-p10-bridge
lec05kp10en-u01-p10-bridge.text: Two parallel boundaries form three bands, below the upper bound of four. What other routes select network size?

lec05kp10en-u01-p10-next-question.name: u01-p10-next-question
lec05kp10en-u01-p10-next-question.text: Does the source sine demo provide a universal size?

lec05kp10en-u01-p10-card1.name: u01-p10-card1
lec05kp10en-u01-p10-card1.text: **Analytical methods** estimate capacity using algebra or statistics, often without optimization details.

lec05kp10en-u01-p10-card2.name: u01-p10-card2
lec05kp10en-u01-p10-card2.text: **Pruning** fits a larger network, then removes less useful connections by a rule.

lec05kp10en-u01-p10-card3.name: u01-p10-card3
lec05kp10en-u01-p10-card3.text: **Constructive methods** grow units from a small architecture. All routes need validation; the next KP studies pruning.

lec05kp10en-u01-p11-title.name: u01-p11-title
lec05kp10en-u01-p11-title.text: Extension: the 1–k–1 demo is one experiment

lec05kp10en-u01-p11-bridge.name: u01-p11-bridge
lec05kp10en-u01-p11-bridge.text: Analytical methods, pruning and constructive methods still need held-out assessment. Does the source sine demo provide a universal size?

lec05kp10en-u01-p11-next-question.name: u01-p11-next-question
lec05kp10en-u01-p11-next-question.text: Can you apply validation selection and cell counting to new numbers?

lec05kp10en-u01-p11-fig1.name: fig:lec05-kp10-trend
lec05kp10en-u01-p11-fig1.text: 同一批帶雜訊的樣本與平滑規律；折線僅作教學示意，不是網路訓練結果。

image.alt: A smooth sine trend and six illustrative noisy samples; the piecewise interpolant is not a fitted neural network.

lec05kp10en-u01-p11-card1.name: u01-p11-card1
lec05kp10en-u01-p11-card1.text: The source uses 15 training points and 10 independent test points for $y=\sin(2\pi x)+\epsilon$, where $\epsilon$ is observation noise.

lec05kp10en-u01-p11-card2.name: u01-p11-card2
lec05kp10en-u01-p11-card2.text: $\hat y=\sum_{j=1}^{k}v_j\tanh(a_jx+b_j)+c$. Adjustable a, b, v and c give $3k+1$ parameters; k counts hidden units.

lec05kp10en-u01-p11-card3.name: u01-p11-card3
lec05kp10en-u01-p11-card3.text: The source describes k around 3–5 as useful and possible overfitting at k=15. These are not universal choices; this training was not rerun here.

lec05kp10en-u01-p12-title.name: u01-p12-title
lec05kp10en-u01-p12-title.text: Extension: choose a checkpoint and explain the cell bound

lec05kp10en-u01-p12-bridge.name: u01-p12-bridge
lec05kp10en-u01-p12-bridge.text: The source sine demo gives no universal k. Can you apply validation selection and cell counting to new numbers?

lec05kp10en-u01-p12-card1.name: u01-p12-card1
lec05kp10en-u01-p12-card1.text: Question 1: training losses are $0.40,0.20,0.10$ and validation losses $0.45,0.25,0.30$. Choose a checkpoint by the validation minimum.

lec05kp10en-u01-p12-card2.name: u01-p12-card2
lec05kp10en-u01-p12-card2.text: Question 2: count the maximum cells of three planar lines in general position using $\binom30+\binom31+\binom32$. Does parallelism attain it?

lec05kp10en-u01-p13-title.name: u01-p13-title
lec05kp10en-u01-p13-title.text: Extension: checkpoint 2 is best; seven is a maximum

lec05kp10en-u01-p13-bridge.name: u01-p13-bridge
lec05kp10en-u01-p13-bridge.text: Question 1 asks for a validation minimum; question 2 counts three planar lines in general position. What do the steps give?

lec05kp10en-u01-p13-next-question.name: u01-p13-next-question
lec05kp10en-u01-p13-next-question.text: Can you recompute an example and state its limits?

lec05kp10en-u01-p13-fig1.name: fig:lec05-kp10-regions
lec05kp10en-u01-p13-fig1.text: 不同輸入維度 d 下，K 個一般位置超平面形成區域數的最大值。

image.alt: Maximum hyperplane cell counts versus hidden-unit count for input dimensions one, two and three.

lec05kp10en-u01-p13-card1.name: u01-p13-card1
lec05kp10en-u01-p13-card1.text: 1. The minimum of $0.45,0.25,0.30$ is $0.25$: retain checkpoint 2, despite lower final training loss.

lec05kp10en-u01-p13-card2.name: u01-p13-card2
lec05kp10en-u01-p13-card2.text: 2. Three planar lines give $M_{\max}=1+3+3=7$. Three parallel lines give only four bands.

lec05kp10en-u01-p13-card3.name: u01-p13-card3
lec05kp10en-u01-p13-card3.text: 3. Validation loss rises by $0.30-0.25=0.05$. Cell count did not enter the checkpoint comparison.

steps.label: Size and fit
steps.speakerNotes: Level: third-year undergraduate. Intended for self-study outside the 270-minute class.

steps.label: Training is not test
steps.speakerNotes:
Previous page: Self-study entry.
Ask the reader to predict at an unobserved position. Similar training fits can disagree there. The diagram is illustrative, not a network experiment.
Next page: Memorizing training answers differs from generalization. Which adjustable numbers give three hidden units their flexibility?
Source: Ch04 KP10, 4.9; focus 1: A perfect training score need not survive new data.

steps.label: Count parameters
steps.speakerNotes:
Previous page: A perfect training score need not survive new data.
Locate the bias represented by each added one. Unit count and adjustable-parameter count differ. Next ask what those degrees of freedom can fit.
Next page: Our three hidden units use thirteen free parameters. Does increasing this count always improve prediction?
Source: Ch04 KP10, 4.9; focus 2: Count adjustable parameters before choosing network size.

steps.label: Fit and noise
steps.speakerNotes:
Previous page: Count adjustable parameters before choosing network size.
A coarse map may omit roads; excessive detail may preserve temporary obstacles. The analogy concerns detail selection, not a claim that every detail is noise.
Next page: Overfitting adapts to incidental training details. Can a fixed architecture do that merely by continuing to train?
Source: Ch04 KP10, 4.9; focus 3: Too little flexibility misses rules; too much can fit noise.

steps.label: Training can overfit
steps.speakerNotes:
Previous page: Too little flexibility misses rules; too much can fit noise.
These five values are a teaching table, not a published experiment. Locate the minimum before asking why the final epoch may not be best.
Next page: Validation loss rises after its minimum at epoch 3 while training loss falls. Which checkpoint should we keep?
Source: Ch04 KP10, 4.9; focus 4: Even a fixed network can worsen with more training.

steps.label: Checkpoint 3 wins
steps.speakerNotes:
Previous page: Even a fixed network can worsen with more training.
Minimize a loss, but maximize an accuracy. Save the actual best weights; reporting epoch 3 while retaining epoch 5 is not restoration.
Next page: Early stopping restores the best checkpoint, here epoch 3. Can repeatedly inspected validation data also give an untouched final score?
Source: Ch04 KP10, 4.9; focus 5: Keep checkpoint 3, not the last checkpoint.

steps.label: Three data roles
steps.speakerNotes:
Previous page: Keep checkpoint 3, not the last checkpoint.
Explain three roles without implying equal split sizes. The source groups validation and test terminology; this material distinguishes their modern roles.
Next page: Training fits weights and validation selects size and checkpoints. With only ten validation cases, how stable is that selection?
Source: Ch04 KP10, 4.9; focus 6: Model selection and final testing need different roles.

steps.label: Tiny validation
steps.speakerNotes:
Previous page: Model selection and final testing need different roles.
Read 0.1 and 0.2 as proportions. The example illustrates sensitivity, not a confidence interval or a guarantee that cross-validation removes all bias.
Next page: One case changes a ten-case estimate by ten percentage points. Can geometry complement this unstable data-based assessment?
Source: Ch04 KP10, 4.9; focus 7: A tiny validation set makes selection unstable.

steps.label: Cell-count bound
steps.speakerNotes:
Previous page: A tiny validation set makes selection unstable.
Count input-space cells, not output classes or guaranteed separable labellings. Distinguish this capacity question from the output separability of KP03.
Next page: The cell-count bound counts possible cells, not output classes. Do two parallel XOR boundaries attain the maximum?
Source: Ch04 KP10, 4.9; focus 8: Geometry counts possible cells, not predictive quality.

steps.label: Parallel XOR bands
steps.speakerNotes:
Previous page: Geometry counts possible cells, not predictive quality.
There are three binomial terms; four is their sum. Separate a capacity check from a constructive sufficiency proof.
Next page: Two parallel boundaries form three bands, below the upper bound of four. What other routes select network size?
Source: Ch04 KP10, 4.9; focus 9: Two planar lines give at most four cells, but parallel lines give three.

steps.label: Three size routes
steps.speakerNotes:
Previous page: Two planar lines give at most four cells, but parallel lines give three.
Contrast shrinking and growing searches. Neither automatically finds the smallest network; computation, stability and interpretability also matter.
Next page: Analytical methods, pruning and constructive methods still need held-out assessment. Does the source sine demo provide a universal size?
Source: Ch04 KP10, 4.9; focus 10: Estimate size, prune a large network, or grow a small one.

steps.label: Extension: sine demo
steps.speakerNotes:
Previous page: Estimate size, prune a large network, or grow a small one.
Tanh smoothly maps a number between minus one and one. Repeatedly choosing k from the test points uses them for selection.
Next page: The source sine demo gives no universal k. Can you apply validation selection and cell counting to new numbers?
Source: Ch04 KP10, 4.9; focus 11: Extension: the 1–k–1 demo is one experiment.

steps.label: Extension: practice
steps.speakerNotes:
Previous page: Extension: the 1–k–1 demo is one experiment.
Answer model selection and geometric counting separately. More cells do not imply lower validation loss. Write a reason before viewing the worked answer.
Next page: Question 1 asks for a validation minimum; question 2 counts three planar lines in general position. What do the steps give?
Source: Ch04 KP10, 4.9; focus 12: Extension: choose a checkpoint and explain the cell bound.

steps.label: Extension: answers
steps.speakerNotes:
Previous page: Extension: choose a checkpoint and explain the cell bound.
Close by asking what is missing when training is perfect but new-data performance is unknown: held-out evidence, not another parameter count.
Next page: Return to the practice and state the assumptions in your own words.
Source: Ch04 KP10, 4.9; focus 13: Extension: checkpoint 2 is best; seven is a maximum.
